definition.simple: Old ways of watering plants using animals or human power to pull water from wells or rivers.
definition.academic: Ancient and historically prevalent methods of supplying water to crops, relying on human labor, animal power, and gravity rather than fossil fuels or electricity.

examples: Using a pulley system (Moat) to lift water from a well.

common_misconceptions: Traditional methods are no longer used anywhere.
ai_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student to imagine farming without electricity, how would they get water out of a deep well?
